q: The quantity that determines how cold or hot an object is is _____.
e: The quantity that determines how cold or hot an object is is temperature. Temperature here means how hot or cold a body is. Heat: energy that flows because of a temperature difference.

q: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called _____.
e: To measure temperature accurately, we use instruments called thermometers. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred involving instruments.

q: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as _____.
e: The energy exchanged between an object and its surrounding due to different temperatures is defined as heat. Heat here means energy that flows because of a temperature difference. Internal energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Heat is the energy in _____.
e: Heat is the energy in transit. Heat is energy on the move; it is not the same word as temperature.

q: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the _____ to the second body.
e: When a body at a higher temperature is in contact with a body at a lower temperature, heat flows from the first body to the second body. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the _____ of that matter.
e: The total energy, that is, the sum of the potential energy and the kinetic energy, of molecules in matter is in fact the internal energy of that matter. Internal energy here means the capacity to do work. Thermal energy: the capacity to do work.

q: Temperature is a measure of the _____ energy of molecules.
e: Temperature is a measure of the internal energy of molecules. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred. Kinetic: energy a body has because it is moving.

q: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with temperature, referred to as the _____ property.
e: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with temperature, referred to as the thermometric property. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the _____ of the liquid.
e: The thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the thermal expansion of the liquid. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: A liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a _____ tube with a narrow bore.
e: A liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a capillary tube with a narrow bore. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary.

q: When the bulb of a liquid-in-glass thermometer becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid is forced into the _____.
e: When the bulb of a liquid-in-glass thermometer becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid is forced into the capillary tube. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary tube.

q: The thinner the _____ wall is, the faster the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes.
e: The thinner the bulb wall is, the faster the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred involving response.

q: The liquid used in a liquid-in-glass thermometer usually contains mercury or coloured _____.
e: The liquid used in a liquid-in-glass thermometer usually contains mercury or coloured alcohol. The physics in this sentence is built around alcohol.

q: Alcohol has a _____ freezing point than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements.
e: Alcohol has a lower freezing point than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the _____ that develops when two different metals are in contact.
e: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the voltage that develops when two different metals are in contact. The physics in this sentence is built around voltage. Current: the flow of electric charge.

q: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure _____ changing temperatures.
e: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure rapidly changing temperatures. The physics in this sentence is built around rapidly involving thermocouple.

q: Thermocouple thermometers can be used to measure much _____ temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers.
e: Thermocouple thermometers can be used to measure much higher temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers. The physics in this sentence is built around higher.

q: A resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical _____ of a metal wire increases with temperature.
e: A resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical resistance of a metal wire increases with temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range _____ to 1200°C.
e: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range -200°C to 1200°C. The physics in this sentence is built around -200°C.

q: A resistance thermometer is best for _____ temperatures, but it is bulky.
e: A resistance thermometer is best for steady temperatures, but it is bulky. The physics in this sentence is built around steady.

q: The SI unit of temperature is _____.
e: The SI unit of temperature is kelvin. SI writes every quantity as a number times an agreed unit.

q: To calibrate a thermometer, two _____ points are chosen and the interval between these points is subdivided.
e: To calibrate a thermometer, two reference points are chosen and the interval between these points is subdivided. The physics in this sentence is built around reference.

q: The freezing point and boiling point of water under normal _____ pressure are chosen as reference points.
e: The freezing point and boiling point of water under normal atmospheric pressure are chosen as reference points. The same force on a smaller area means a larger pressure. Standard: the reference you compare length, mass, or time against.

q: On the Celsius scale, the ice point is _____ and the steam point is 100°C.
e: On the Celsius scale, the ice point is 0°C and the steam point is 100°C. The physics in this sentence is built around 0°C.

q: On the Fahrenheit scale, the ice point is 32°F and the steam point is _____.
e: On the Fahrenheit scale, the ice point is 32°F and the steam point is 212°F. The physics in this sentence is built around 212°F.

q: On the Kelvin scale, the ice point is 273 K and the steam point is _____.
e: On the Kelvin scale, the ice point is 273 K and the steam point is 373 K. The physics in this sentence is built around 373 K.

q: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_C$ and the Fahrenheit temperature $T_F$ is given by the equation $T_F = $ _____.
e: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_C$ and the Fahrenheit temperature $T_F$ is given by the equation $T_F = $ $1.8 T_C + 32$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_C$ and kelvin temperature $T_K$ is given by $T_K = $ _____.
e: The relationship between the Celsius temperature $T_C$ and kelvin temperature $T_K$ is given by $T_K = $ $T_C + 273$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: Normal body temperature is 98.6°F, which is _____ on the Celsius scale.
e: Normal body temperature is 98.6°F, which is 37.0°C on the Celsius scale. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: When a substance is heated, its volume usually increases. This phenomenon is known as _____.
e: When a substance is heated, its volume usually increases. This phenomenon is known as thermal expansion. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: The increase in size of a heated substance can be explained in terms of the increased _____ energy of the molecules.
e: The increase in size of a heated substance can be explained in terms of the increased kinetic energy of the molecules. Kinetic here means energy a body has because it is moving. Potential: stored energy due to position or shape.

q: The dependence of the change in length of an object on its original length and change in temperature is $\Delta l = $ _____.
e: The dependence of the change in length of an object on its original length and change in temperature is $\Delta l = $ $\alpha l \Delta T$. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: In the linear expansion formula, $\alpha$ represents the coefficient of _____ expansion.
e: In the linear expansion formula, $\alpha$ represents the coefficient of linear expansion. The physics in this sentence is built around linear.

q: The unit of the coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is per K, which can be written as _____.
e: The unit of the coefficient of linear expansion $\alpha$ is per K, which can be written as $K^{-1}$. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: The coefficient of linear expansion is the change in length per _____ length for one degree change in temperature.
e: The coefficient of linear expansion is the change in length per unit length for one degree change in temperature. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.

q: The relation for area expansion is $\Delta A = $ _____.
e: The relation for area expansion is $\Delta A = $ $\beta A \Delta T$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\beta A \Delta T$.

q: In the area expansion equation, $\beta$ is the coefficient of _____ expansion.
e: In the area expansion equation, $\beta$ is the coefficient of area expansion. The physics in this sentence is built around area.

q: The relation for volume expansion is $\Delta V = $ _____.
e: The relation for volume expansion is $\Delta V = $ $\gamma V \Delta T$. The physics in this sentence is built around $\gamma V \Delta T$.

q: The coefficient of volume expansion of a substance is the change in volume per _____ volume for one degree change in temperature.
e: The coefficient of volume expansion of a substance is the change in volume per unit volume for one degree change in temperature. Unit here means an agreed amount you use as the scale of a measurement.

q: Generally all substances expand on heating and contract on cooling, but water shows _____ expansion.
e: Generally all substances expand on heating and contract on cooling, but water shows anomalous expansion. The physics in this sentence is built around anomalous.

q: When water at 0°C is heated, its volume decreases up to _____ and density increases.
e: When water at 0°C is heated, its volume decreases up to 4°C and density increases. Density compares mass with the space that mass occupies.

q: At 4°C, the _____ of water becomes maximum.
e: At 4°C, the density of water becomes maximum. Density here means mass per unit volume.
